lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Auto Parts | Mechanical Design Engineer | Metro City, Country | Jun 2025 - Present
- Designed stamping dies for automotive brackets in SolidWorks, cutting the scrap rate from 6% to 4% on two press lines.
- Ran tolerance stack-up analyses for 12 production parts and signed off first-article inspections with the supplier.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: State a clear target role near the top.
items.because: Readers currently have to infer whether you are pursuing mechanical design, robotics, ML engineering, or agent systems.

items.says: Consider a short professional summary connecting your ML and robotics experience to your target role.
items.because: The résumé does not summarize your ML profile.

items.says: Explain the overlapping work and study dates where necessary.
items.because: The M.S., ML internship, and current mechanical role overlap and may prompt questions about the arrangement.

items.says: Use consistent location and date formatting across entries.
items.because: The education entries use different country formats, and the résumé mixes an expected date with completed ranges.

items.says: Expand the brief skills section with substantiated, role-relevant technologies where useful.
items.because: It is sparse relative to the technical detail in the experience section.

items.says: Check wrapped bullets, spacing, and page breaks in the rendered document.
items.because: The supplied text does not show whether the layout is easy to scan.

items.says: Use a consistent visual treatment for dates, locations, titles, and project details.
items.because: The supplied text does not show the typography or page fill.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not needed to evaluate qualifications and introduces irrelevant personal information into screening.

items.says: Remove nationality unless a specific application requires it.
items.because: Relevant work authorization should be communicated directly instead.

items.says: Clarify the expected graduation date and current enrollment status.
items.because: The degree is in progress, so that status should be unambiguous.

items.says: Reconsider the prominence of the current mechanical role for an ML application.
items.because: Leading with its title and duties may make the résumé appear less ML-focused.

items.says: Differentiate this loss-masking contribution from the later loss-masking bullet.
items.because: The two bullets appear to describe the same method and may make the internship seem padded.

items.says: Clarify the baseline, measurement method, and test conditions for the 35% accuracy improvement.
items.because: A reviewer may ask how the result was established.

items.says: Clarify the basis for the reviewer-disagreement reduction.
items.because: A reviewer may ask about its baseline, measurement method, and test conditions.

items.says: Clarify how the tool-call and latency reductions were measured.
items.because: A reviewer may ask about their baselines and test conditions.

items.says: Differentiate this loss-masking bullet from the earlier one.
items.because: They appear to describe the same method rather than distinct contributions.

items.says: The triage system and backlog result are repeated under a project.
items.because: Presenting the same achievement under two headings can look like double-counting.

items.says: Clarify what you personally delivered and how the backlog impact was measured.
items.because: Saying the system launched does not establish your ownership or the impact measurement.

items.says: Add context to the 4× GPU-memory reduction.
items.because: A reviewer may ask which memory measure, workload, and model configuration were compared.

items.says: Correct the shift from “Maintained” to “adds.”
items.because: The bullet combines past and present tense.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the broad adoption and outcomes claim.
items.because: It does not show what changed, how adoption was measured, or which outcomes improved.

items.says: Clarify the 100× context-growth comparison and 10K-token measurement.
items.because: A technical reader will want to know what grew and how the limit was measured.

items.says: Clarify your contribution as a “Contributor.”
items.because: The bullets should distinguish your work from the framework’s overall capabilities.

items.says: The triage system and backlog result repeat the internship achievement.
items.because: Repeating the same result under two headings can look like double-counting.

items.says: Verify that the sensor-triage bullet belongs under this project.
items.because: It seems unrelated to the Research-Agent Evaluation Framework title and other bullets.

items.says: Organize the skills categories around the target role.
items.because: “ML & Agents” currently combines tools, methods, and a broad capability.
